overview.description: The miniprep is the premier method for purifying plasmid DNA - doable in under two hours with the right set-up. It uses some nasty chemicals (guanidine), so read the MSDS. A high-speed centrifuge is the single most important piece of equipment here.
objectives: perform a silica-column miniprep end to end
judge plasmid yield (gel is more reliable than nanodrop)

steps.description: The miniprep is the premier method for purifying plasmid DNA - doable in under two hours with the right set-up. It uses some nasty chemicals (guanidine), so read the MSDS. A high-speed centrifuge is the single most important piece of equipment here.
steps.intro: The miniprep is the premier method for purifying plasmid DNA - doable in under two hours with the right set-up. It uses some nasty chemicals (guanidine), so read the MSDS. A high-speed centrifuge is the single most important piece of equipment here.

instructions.title: Pellet & resuspend
instructions.description: Spin down an overnight culture and resuspend the pellet in resuspension buffer.

instructions.title: Lyse & neutralise
instructions.description: Add lysis buffer, wait ~10 min so RNAse degrades RNA, then neutralise and spin to pellet debris.

instructions.title: Bind to column
instructions.description: Load the cleared supernatant onto a silica column and spin to capture plasmid DNA.

instructions.title: Wash & dry
instructions.description: Wash with chaotropic salt then ethanol; dry in an oven to evaporate residual ethanol.

instructions.title: Elute
instructions.description: Add elution buffer and spin into a fresh tube. Store at -20C.

submission.description: Miniprep a plasmid and report your yield. Verify quality by running an aliquot on an agarose gel.
